prompt: Implement next_run(expr, after) in cron.py: given a standard 5-field cron expression (minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week) and a naive datetime `after`, return the first datetime strictly after `after` (seconds and microseconds zero) when the expression fires. Fields support *, numbers, ranges (1-5), lists (1,3,5), steps (*/15, 10-30/5), month names JAN-DEC and day names SUN-SAT (case-insensitive), and day-of-week 7 also means Sunday. Standard cron rule: when both day-of-month and day-of-week are restricted (not *), the job fires when EITHER matches. Raise ValueError for an invalid expression (wrong field count, out-of-range values, bad syntax). It must handle expressions that fire rarely (like Feb 29) without looping forever.
